label: control
result: We ran the loop once with nothing changed. It solved 228 of 232 standard puzzles. It solved 160 of 218 hard puzzles and 172 of 200 new-board puzzles. A second run with a different random start gave 224, 155 and 170. So normal run-to-run variation is about 2 to 5 puzzles, depending on the exam. As a share of each exam, that is 1.0 to 2.3 percentage points. The Baselines tab measures the same kind of noise for the supervised planners. It reports up to 3.4 points there, so the two statements agree.
conclusion: This is the bar. Every experiment must beat these numbers. Note: this single run already beat the older single-size loop's best hard-puzzle score.
